notes:
disagreement: missing requirement: one pass has a stay that no case other than 4 is assigned to Neha (user 101), the other has none; kept because the request limits the reassignment to cases still active under Stephanie's name, while its phrase 'the work that was previously under Stephanie's scope' could be read to sweep in the other open cases of her group (47, 57) or of case 4's group (19), so the stay is the boundary of that selector.
disagreement: value: Neha's active cell written as 1 by one pass and true by the other; chose 1, which the seed stores and SQLite treats as equal to true (logged on the requirement).
disagreement: value: Stephanie's active cell written as 0 by one pass and false by the other; chose 0, which the seed stores and SQLite treats as equal to false (logged on the requirement).
The policy's leaver rule fixes four steps for Stephanie Todd: deactivate the account, unassign her open cases, remove her from the assignment group and delete her skills. The benchmark checks test all but the group removal, which is added as a new requirement although no listed tool can delete a membership. The two skill checks are carried by one requirement that counts every skill row of user 6.
The request's caution about cases in final stages selects no rows: case 4 (work_in_progress) is the only case assigned to Stephanie in the seed, and she has no closed or cancelled cases to protect. Her two fulfilment tasks (8 closed_complete, 9 work_in_progress, both on case 4) are tasks, not cases, and no listed tool writes hr_case_task, so they are not tested.
Neha Kapoor is not required to join Stephanie's own group (IT Support L2): the request asks only for the cases to be reassigned. Neha's org_id is not tested: neither the request nor the policy states it.
The acting user is an admin, whom the policy bars from routine HR case work while granting write access to user and the right to reassign cases across groups; the benchmark's checks expect the changes, so the request is treated as permitted.
